description: How one automaker rode the EV mania to trillion-dollar dreams while a swarm of hyped rivals went from IPO stardom to rubble. This timeline traces real market-cap highs and epic collapses driven by SPAC fever, production reality, supply-chain shocks and Tesla's runaway scale advantage (2007–2026).
youtube_description:
The EV Hype Crash — a chart-race of boom and bust.

Story in one sentence: Tesla went from niche EV builder to the scale titan of the auto era while Rivian, Lucid and Nikola rode IPO/SPAC mania into sky-high market caps and then crashed back to earth when production, margins and reality arrived.

What you’ll see in this visualization:
- Early years: Tesla is tiny or private while legacy manufacturing dominates.
- 2012–2019: Tesla scales with the Model S/3/Y lineup and steadily gains market value.
- 2020–2021: SPAC and IPO fever + EV optimism send Rivian and Lucid into astronomic valuations; Nikola also spikes after a 2020 SPAC run.
- 2022–2024: Production struggles, cutbacks, accounting & fraud investigations (Nikola), slower-than-expected deliveries, supply-chain shocks and rising interest rates crush valuations.
- 2025–2026: A clearer separation — Tesla keeps scaling (manufacturing, FSD bets, energy business) while the formerly-hyped names struggle for viable margins.

Sources and context: public market caps, IPO/SPAC filings and widely reported peak valuations from 2020–2022; known events include Rivian and Lucid 2021 public listings, Nikola's 2020 SPAC peak and subsequent scandals, and Tesla's scaling driven by Model 3/Y volume and global gigafactory expansion. Values are shown in billions USD (market cap snapshots by year) to illustrate the narrative of one winner scaling and several contestants collapsing.
